param: seqsubsky DEGREE applied to the sky flat's SOURCE frames only: 1 (control, shipped) vs 2 (arm). The LIGHTS keep degree 1 in both arms — that is the knob NOT being turned, so unresolved-starlight preservation in the deliverable is unchanged and the comparison isolates the flat.
control: web/results/july31/stack_set-01_spcc.fit, built on skyflat_set-01_desky.fit (degree 1). Regional Siril stat, 400px boxes, 200px margin: centre G=100.4, TL 105.7, TR 94.0, BL 104.7, BR 99.8 -> TL/TR = 1.124.
hypothesis: The residual gradient is the moon's sky term retained in the FLAT, not real sky and not the warp. Degree 1 fits a plane; a 93.8%-illuminated moon 54.9 deg off-axis imposes CURVATURE the plane cannot reach, so it survives into the flat and calibration stamps its INVERSE on every light. Predicts: at degree 2 the flat's corner spread falls from 1.099 toward ~1.0, the stack's TL/TR falls from 1.124 toward ~1.03 (the 3.10% level the --desky commit priced as the accepted residual), and the anti-correlation between region brightness and moon separation (currently a near-perfect inverse ordering, rho ~ -1) collapses. FALSIFIED IF the stack's corner spread is unchanged or worsens, or the moon anti-correlation survives at full strength -- either would mean the gradient is not flat-borne and the flat is not the place to fix it.
why_degree_2_is_allowed_here: The degree-1 constraint exists to protect frame-filling UNRESOLVED STARLIGHT (dead-ends terminology, sense 2) in the LIGHTS. In the FLAT that same structure is contamination, not signal: it is fixed on the celestial sphere, the mount is fixed, so it drifts across the sensor and rejects out of an un-registered stack anyway. Protecting it there protects nothing and retains the moon term.
measures: brightness vs galactic latitude ordering (real MW must peak at b=0)
verdict: FALSIFIED, and not for the reason the hypothesis guarded against. Degree 2 did remove the sky curvature — and it removed the VIGNETTING with it. The flat's corner/centre ratio went 0.513-0.563 (a real vignetting profile) to 0.937-1.006 (no vignetting at all), so the product the flat exists to carry was gone. Reason: PARITY. Vignetting is an EVEN, radial function of position; a degree-1 plane is odd-plus-constant, so it CANNOT touch the radial term by construction — which is exactly why the --desky commit measured radial vignetting preserved to 0.3115 -> 0.3114 at degree 1. Degree 2 is the first degree with even terms, and those are the SAME functional form as vignetting, so subsky cannot separate them: it subtracts the vignetting from every source frame and the stacked flat comes out flat. Degree 1 is therefore not a compromise between sky removal and signal preservation — it is the ONLY degree that separates the sky TILT from the vignetting, and no degree can remove sky CURVATURE from a flat without removing the flat. The residual the --desky commit priced ('the gradient's CURVATURE, which degree 1 cannot reach and degree 2 must not touch') is IRREDUCIBLE at this stage. july31's 12.4% is that irreducible term, inflated ~4x over july23's 3.10% by a 93.8%-lit moon 54.9 deg off-axis. It is an ACQUISITION problem; the fix is not in the flat.

metrics.gate_deg2: FAILS the builder's own gate 'smooth falloff (corners < centre)': BL reads 1.006 of centre.
metrics.stack_arm: NOT BUILT — stopped at the flat. Feeding a vignetting-free flat into a stack measures arithmetic, not the hypothesis.

falsified_premise: The pre-registered reasoning — 'in the flat the diffuse field is contamination, so a higher degree is safe there' — is still TRUE about starlight and still irrelevant: the blocker is the vignetting, which the hypothesis never considered.
knob_disposition: --desky-degree reverted; a flag whose only non-default value destroys the product is a footgun, and the finding lives in docs/dead-ends.md instead.

param: seqsubsky on the FLAT's source frames: ON (shipped --desky) vs OFF. The LIGHTS keep --desky in both arms — their subsky runs AFTER flat division, on flat-fielded data, which is the domain subsky is defined for. Only the flat build changes.
control: stack_set-01_spcc.fit on skyflat_set-01_desky.fit. Edge dipole-X (medians, box 80, normalised to the 4-corner mean): +0.139 at 42px from edge; corner spread 12.4%; BL 96.0 vs BR 118.2.
hypothesis: seqsubsky subtracts an ADDITIVE plane from frames that still carry MULTIPLICATIVE vignetting. The frame is sky x V, not sky; V falls to ~35% at the corners, so a linear fit overshoots hardest where curvature is steepest — at the frame edge — and drives the local asymmetry through zero. MEASURED support: raw dark-subtracted light +0.426/+0.449/+0.490 at 42/90/290px; pre---desky flat +0.365/+0.359/+0.398 (same sign, ~85% of magnitude, i.e. it CORRECTLY captured the optical asymmetry); --desky flats -0.550/-0.415/-0.060 (july31) and -0.441/-0.335/+0.019 (july14) — sign INVERTED in both sessions. Master dark +0.000, so not the dark. Predicts: with the flat built WITHOUT subsky, the stack's edge dipole collapses toward 0 and the BL/BR corner reversal disappears.
falsified_if: the stack's edge dipole is unchanged or grows, which would mean the flat's inverted edge is not what puts the reversal into the product and the cause is downstream (warp/registration/framing).
expected_cost: the sky term returns to the flat, so object photometry regains the multiplicative tilt the --desky commit measured at 3.11% / 241 sigma. This arm isolates the EDGE defect; it is not proposed as the shipped configuration.
